genre_name: Systematic review and meta-analysis of adverse events from randomized trials (drug-safety signal / repurposing screen)
scope: Systematic reviews that pool harm or adverse-event outcomes (or an unintended benefit used as a repurposing signal) for a drug or drug class across randomized controlled trials, usually placebo- or active-controlled, reporting pooled RR/OR/rate ratios (sometimes risk differences), heterogeneity, risk of bias and, ideally, certainty of evidence. Core: pairwise aggregate-data meta-analysis of published RCTs (6/8). Covered variants: one network meta-analysis of harms (E3), one individual-participant-data meta-analysis of double-blind trials (E4, CTT) and one benefit-harm review where harms are co-primary (E8). Not covered: meta-analyses of observational or pharmacovigilance data, single-arm incidence pooling, Cochrane reviews, efficacy-only reviews, protocols.
word_count_convention: jats_structure.py prose words (post-12:31 fix); captions, table footnotes, boxed text, formulas, numeric citations and headings excluded; main = I+M+R+D(+L,C); limitations subsections are counted inside Discussion

sections.heading: Abstract

Form and length are set by the venue profile: JAMA Key Points 77-85 words (Question/Findings/Meaning); BMJ box 138 words; Lancet-family Research in context 412-513 words (Evidence before this study / Added value / Implications; includes a search description); AHA Clinical Perspective 88 words; PLOS Author summary 226 words.

standard_items.text: Harm definitions, grading and ascertainment differed across trials; AEs were investigator-reported rather than systematically collected, risking misclassification and under-reporting
Aggregate trial-level data only; no individual participant data, so patient-level subgroups (sex, age, mutation type, comorbidity) could not be examined
Clinical and methodological diversity across trials (populations, comparators, co-interventions, follow-up) and statistical heterogeneity
Rare events, low event rates and underpowered subgroups give imprecise estimates; RCTs are not designed to detect rare harms
Different agents, doses or formulations pooled as one class
Unpublished trials or unreported harm outcomes missing; possible selective reporting
Unequal follow-up or exposure time between arms; crude cumulative counts rather than exposure-adjusted rates
Trial participants are more selected and healthier than real-world users (and may exclude prior intolerance), so harms may be underestimated

variation_notes: Venue house style, not design, drives most variation. Length is bimodal: JAMA Netw Open, JAHA and EHJ-CVP papers run 2300-3300 words with 500-700-word Methods, while BMJ, Lancet, eClinicalMedicine and PLOS Medicine run 5100-5400 words with 970-1900-word Methods. JAMA, BMJ and PLOS use outcome-wise Results subheadings; Lancet family, AHA and ESC write Results as unheaded paragraphs. Separate Conclusions appear only in JAMA and ESC (BMJ nests them). Every venue but EHJ-CVP adds its own summary layer. The Lancet family puts 'Role of the funding source' inside Methods and 'Funding' in the abstract. Reporting rigour also varies independently of venue tier: registration 4/8, RoB 2 4/8, GRADE/CINeMA 2/8, PRISMA 2020 cited 2/8; E1 (JAMA Netw Open 2022) has no registration, funding or data statement, E6 (JAHA 2024) has no registration or RoB tool, and E8 (PLOS Medicine) has no registration and uses the Jadad score. Design variants: NMA (E3) adds network geometry, CINeMA, heatmaps and PRISMA-NMA; IPD collaboration (E4) drops PRISMA/flow/RoB and adds ethics approval, Peto-type O-E statistics and absolute excess per 1000 person-years; the benefit-harm review (E8) doubles the forest plots and adds NNT/NNH.
lint_notes: Title must name drug/class, harm outcome and design ('systematic review and meta-analysis', ideally 'of randomised controlled trials').

Abstract must give number of trials and participants and a pooled ratio with 95% CI for the primary harm; check the PRISMA-A items exemplars often miss (risk of bias, registration, funding, limitations of evidence).
Every harm forest plot needs per-arm events/total, the ratio measure on a log axis with a reference line at 1, a pooled diamond, the model name and I2 (plus tau2 or Q p value) in the plot or caption.
Methods must define each harm outcome with its dictionary (CTCAE, MedDRA, ISTH/BARC or trial definitions) and grade/seriousness, and say whether AEs are treatment-related or treatment-emergent.

For rare harms, Methods must state zero-event handling (Peto OR or Mantel-Haenszel without correction, continuity correction as sensitivity); only 2/8 exemplars do, but its absence is a reviewer flag.
Report absolute effects (risk difference, events per 1000, or NNH) next to relative effects; a GRADE summary-of-findings table satisfies this and PRISMA item 22 in one display item.
PRISMA flow diagram may sit in the supplement (JAMA) but must exist; the IPD-collaboration variant is the only exemplar without one.
Funnel plot/Egger and RoB figures belong in the supplement; flag funnel plots drawn with fewer than 10 trials.
Limitations block (inside Discussion) must concede heterogeneous AE ascertainment; a missing 'trial-level only' concession should warn for aggregate-data reviews.
Do not count venue summary boxes toward display-item caps; median main-text display items is 5-6 (range 5-10).
Registration ID regex: PROSPERO CRD42 followed by 9-11 digits (e.g. CRD42024517308, CRD420251231682).
notes: Exemplar search: Europe PMC (OPEN_ACCESS, 2022-2026) across JAMA Netw Open, BMJ, Lancet family, PLOS Med, BMC Med, diabetes, cardiology and Drug Safety journals.

Excluded for contamination though otherwise ideal: BMC Medicine semaglutide and tirzepatide harms reviews with Trial Sequential Analysis (pancreatitis/pancreatic outcomes in body), CTT Lancet 2026 statin product-label AE screen (pancreatitis outcome), JAHA 2025 angiogenesis-inhibitor MACE review (pancreatic NET in body), DOM 2025 GLP-1 RA cancer review (cancer outcomes incl. pancreatic). Consequently no exemplar uses Trial Sequential Analysis; tsa_plot is not profiled.
E8 (PLOS Medicine anti-amyloid) is a benefit-harm review with efficacy co-primary; kept for PLOS house style and ARIA harms, but its reporting is weak (Jadad, no registration).
E4 (CTT Lancet 2022) is an IPD meta-analysis of double-blind trials, not a literature-based systematic review; it lowers the frequency of PRISMA, registration, RoB and flow-diagram items.
BMJ visual abstract and possible EHJ-CVP graphical abstract are not in PMC XML and were not counted as figures.
Supplement contents were classified from supplement captions and in-text supplement references; supplement files themselves (PDF/DOCX) were not opened.
Display-item vocabulary: heatmap (E3), absolute-risk figure (E4 Fig 3) and mechanism schematic (E7 Fig 5) are single-exemplar kinds and are recorded only in exemplar measured blocks.
